promised.clause: Successful sync() makes all previously accepted writes in every live WAL generation survive a crash, provided the OS, filesystem and device honor their persistence contract.
A write batch publishes and recovers all its mutations together, without exposing a partial batch.
A captured snapshot keeps its logical view across later writes, flushes and compactions.
A failed WAL sync poisons the engine and blocks further mutations until a successful reopen of valid on-disk state.
WAL records, SST blocks and new versioned MANIFEST envelopes use CRC-32 checksums; legacy unversioned MANIFESTs upgrade on their next install.
Under the simulated device model, recovered state equals some prefix of acknowledged writes that includes every successfully synced write.

Recovery reports corruption without modifying the WAL when a surviving later sync marker with the readable header's private nonce proves damaged bytes were synced; without that proof damage truncates, and deliberate nonce forgery is outside the threat model.
Rotation syncs the closed WAL generation before creating the next, so generations become durable in order.

not_promised.clause: A successful put() or delete() before sync() may be lost after a crash.
Dropping a handle does not acknowledge crash durability.
Concurrent access by two independent processes to one directory is not validated as a supported usage; the OS lock rejects a second owner.
Power loss is simulated with torn writes, directory durability and per-file loss; these suites do not establish behavior on physical hardware.
The API and storage format may change before 1.0.
